_comment: Market-wide positioning collection for signals/positioning.py. Every
setting here is meant to be edited: change a search, a keyword or a
threshold with a commit and the next run uses it. The rules for the
digest and the same-day email are in signals/POSITIONING_SUMMARY.md.
Holdings never go in this file: the repository is public. See
_feed_note: Google News search feed: the same query language as a Google search
(quotes, OR, site:), no account, about 100 newest items per query. The
daily run adds when:3d so a Monday run still covers the weekend; the
backfill adds after:/before: one week at a time.

_note: Which collected stories count. The searches stay verbatim; this filter
decides what is kept for the counts, the dashboard and the digest. The
13-week backfill on 2026-09-25 showed 100 of 180 stories were
MarketBeat auto-generated rating changes and 13F stake notices, nearly
all caught by the JPMorgan search. Every row stays in headlines.csv;
only the counting skips them. A story counts when its outlet is not
excluded and its headline has at least one require_any phrase.

tags._note: Whole-word, case-insensitive matches on the headline. A headline can carry several tags.

_note: How busy prime-brokerage chatter is: the number of distinct stories
this week (Monday to Sunday, U.S. Eastern) compared with the median of
the previous baseline_weeks weeks. A story is counted once however
many outlets carry it or searches catch it. Needs min_weeks of history
Dates computed by rule, in U.S. Eastern time. Estimated windows are
labelled as estimates on the page and in the digest. The FINRA and
FOMC lists override the rule-based dates when filled in; they are
copied from the official pages, never typed from memory.
